models.label: Beta Cephei pulsation
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: Mode geometry and inclination cancellation are not modeled.

models.label: Linear limb-darkened eclipse
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: Uses annular quadrature and bolometric luminosity weights, not atmosphere-specific passbands.
No gravity darkening, spots, or Roche geometry in occultation silhouettes.

models.label: Ellipsoidal and reflection modulation
models.applicability: Detached binary with positive radii, masses and separation.
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: Leading-order detached approximation; disabled implicitly when inputs are invalid.

models.label: Keplerian binary orientation and orbit
models.applicability: Two surviving stellar components with a positive period.
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: Orientation is sampled isotropically; apsidal motion is omitted.

models.label: Classical Cepheid radial pulsation
models.applicability: Inside the mode-specific, metallicity-dependent Cepheid F or 1O strip with 2.7 <= logL <= 4.3.
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: F/1O overlap mode selection remains a population prior because crossing number is unavailable.
The nonlinear F-period calibration covers 3-11 Msun and Z=0.004-0.03; outside it the density relation is retained and flagged.
The transported Z is used as an explicitly flagged proxy for [Fe/H], while 1O periods retain the legacy density relation pending a pooled nonlinear calibration.
The Anderson strip is retained for coherent F+1O coverage; newer nonlinear F edges depend on crossing, convection and overshooting and do not yet supply a like-for-like 1O replacement.
Harmonic amplitudes are population priors, not fitted light curves.

models.label: Cool-star spots and white-light flares
models.applicability: Non-degenerate cool stars; calibrated subset is 0.09-1.36 Msun, logg >= 4 and 3200-6250 K.
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: Rotation, spot coverage and flare rate are inferred population priors.
No spot-crossing anomalies or spatial flare occultation.

models.label: DAV / ZZ Ceti pulsation
models.applicability: Hydrogen-atmosphere WD proxy at 10400-12400 K and 7.5 <= logg <= 9.1, with surface H > 0.1 or unavailable; MIST cross-phase interpolations are excluded.
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: Atmosphere type is inferred when the source evolution data do not provide it.
The surface-H=0.1 atmosphere boundary is a heuristic proxy for a spectral classification.
The observed temperature-gravity box is a population selector, not a star-specific non-adiabatic stability calculation.

models.label: DBV / V777 Her pulsation
models.applicability: Helium-atmosphere WD proxy at 22400-32000 K and 7.5 <= logg <= 8.3, with surface H <= 0.1 or unavailable; MIST cross-phase interpolations are excluded.
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: Atmosphere type is inferred when the source evolution data do not provide it.
The surface-H=0.1 atmosphere boundary is a heuristic proxy for a spectral classification.
The observed temperature-gravity box is a population selector, not a star-specific non-adiabatic stability calculation.

models.label: Delta Scuti / SX Phoenicis multimode pulsation
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: Instability boundaries and amplitude distribution are deliberately broad.

models.label: Gamma Doradus multimode pulsation
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: No rotation-dependent period-spacing pattern.

models.label: GW Vir pulsation
models.applicability: PG1159 proxy with surface H <= 0.1 or unavailable, in either the PNNV domain (100000-180000 K, 5.5 <= logg <= 7.0) or DOV domain (80000-100000 K, 7.3 <= logg <= 7.7); MIST cross-phase interpolations are excluded.
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: MIST surface H is only a proxy for the He/C/O-rich PG1159 atmosphere required for a physical GW Vir classification.
The surface-H=0.1 atmosphere boundary is a heuristic proxy for a spectral classification.
The two observed temperature-gravity boxes are population selectors, not a star-specific non-adiabatic stability calculation.

models.label: Hot-star stochastic low-frequency variability
models.applicability: Non-degenerate stars hotter than 10000 K and more massive than 3 Msun.
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: The amplitude/frequency prior is phenomenological and not a hydrodynamic simulation.

models.label: Low-amplitude fallback microvariability
models.applicability: Any finite photospheric component without another assigned mechanism.
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: This is a visualization floor, not a predicted variability classification.

models.label: Mira-like long-period pulsation
models.applicability: Very cool luminous giants with large radii.
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: Dust, shocks and cycle-to-cycle irregularity are omitted.

models.label: Red-giant oscillations and granulation
models.applicability: Cool evolved stars with logg < 3.5 and L > 5 Lsun.
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: Mixed-mode forests and evolutionary-state-specific spacings are omitted.

models.label: RR Lyrae radial pulsation
models.applicability: Direct core-He-burning, single-phase components on the Marconi A/B horizontal-branch grid with 0.51 <= M/Msun <= 0.80 and 0.0001 <= Z <= 0.02.
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: The continuously interpolated mode topology is restricted to the well-sampled A/B horizontal-branch sequences; sparse evolved C/D sequences fail closed.
Mass is gated only by the published grid envelope, so every emitted record flags the A/B topology as a mass-branch proxy.
F/1O overlap mode selection is a flagged population prior because evolutionary direction is unavailable; RRd pulsation is not represented.
Updated-opacity models do not publish a replacement full grid and imply roughly 100-200 K edge systematics, especially for evolved and metal-rich topology.
DESI empirical edges are validation diagnostics rather than selector replacements because they omit mass, luminosity, helium and evolutionary state.
The source populations do not currently include calibrated RGB mass loss or horizontal-branch morphology and can therefore yield no RR Lyrae stars.
Fractional radius and temperature amplitudes remain explicitly flagged, uncalibrated population priors; Blazhko modulation and shocks are omitted.
Partially stripped binary RR candidates below the classical grid are excluded rather than extrapolated into this model.

models.label: Semiregular red-variable pulsation
models.applicability: Cool luminous giants below the Mira prior threshold.
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: Mode sequences are represented by a broad population prior.

models.label: Solar-like stochastic oscillations
models.applicability: Cool dwarfs and subgiants with finite mass, radius, luminosity and temperature.
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: Random-access phase renewal approximates, rather than integrates, a driven damped oscillator.

models.label: Slowly pulsating B-star variability
models.phaseConvention: t=0 is the stored phase origin; positive phase advances with time.
limitations: Metallicity and rotation shifts of the instability domain are omitted.

populationModels.label: Historical detached-binary Roche screen
populationModels.applicability: Candidate binaries whose two independently evolved MIST component histories are certified from the first finite model through the observation age.
equations: retain iff history_certified and max_t,i(F_i)<0.90 and max_t((R1+R2)/r_peri)<1
populationModels.phaseConvention: No orbital light-curve phase is evaluated: both component histories are compared at coeval stellar ages through the exact observation age.
limitations: The 0.90 Roche-fill cut is a conservative ten-percent certification guard, not a calibrated onset criterion for mass transfer.
Eggleton's circular synchronous Roche radius evaluated at periastron is only an approximation for eccentric or asynchronous systems.
Birth semimajor axis and eccentricity are held fixed; tides, spin coupling, winds, accretion, supernova kicks, and common-envelope evolution are omitted.
When synchronized histories are unavailable, extrema from every bracketing MIST corner form a conservative bound and can reject systems that are actually detached.
A missing, non-finite, extrapolated, or otherwise uncertified component history rejects the whole binary; rejected systems are not replacement-sampled.

populationModels.label: Period-conditioned field eccentricity prior
populationModels.applicability: MIST binary candidates after the canonical birth period is drawn.
equations: the same e_birth is used without clamping by detached screening and orbital photometry
populationModels.phaseConvention: No viewing phase: e is sampled once at birth and the orbital epoch is assigned separately.
limitations: The sharp 12-day field circularization boundary is a population prior, not a tidal-evolution calculation and is applied independent of stellar type and age.
The uniform long-period law approximates solar-type field binaries and omits observed mass, period, and environmental structure.
Extreme-e systems are retained at birth only if the separate full-history periastron Roche/overlap screen certifies them as detached.

populationModels.label: Kroupa primary-mass birth prior
populationModels.applicability: MIST candidate-system primary masses inside the configured supported mass interval.
equations: dN/dM proportional to M^-1.3 for M<0.5 Msun
dN/dM proportional to 0.5*M^-2.3 for M>=0.5 Msun
segment and within-segment draws use exact inverse CDFs
populationModels.phaseConvention: No temporal phase: each draw is a birth primary mass.
limitations: A universal field IMF is applied to every galaxy and cluster profile; environmental IMF variation is omitted.
Primary masses, rather than individual-star masses from an all-star pairing process, are drawn from this IMF.
The MIST production interval starts at 0.1 Msun, while the population weight accounts analytically for the configured full-IMF interval.

populationModels.label: Flat MIST-supported mass-ratio prior
populationModels.applicability: MIST systems selected as binaries and conditioned on two supported stellar tracks.
populationModels.phaseConvention: No temporal phase: q and the secondary birth mass are sampled once.
limitations: This is explicitly the target population conditional on M2>=0.1 Msun, not an intrinsic companion distribution or a completeness correction.
Binary membership is not reduced, replacement-sampled, or weight-corrected for companions below the MIST track floor.
A flat q law omits the mass-, period-, and twin-dependent structure measured in real populations and can overemphasize equal masses near the low-mass track boundary.

populationModels.label: Mass-binned field multiplicity prior
populationModels.applicability: MIST candidate systems using the mass-dependent binary-fraction model.
populationModels.phaseConvention: No temporal phase: membership is sampled once at birth.
limitations: Piecewise fractions summarize heterogeneous field samples and ignore metallicity, age, environment, and hierarchical multiplicity.
The 0.1-0.5 Msun bin is a broad M-dwarf approximation; substellar companions are outside this MIST target population.
The high-mass bins retain a legacy coarse approximation rather than the full correlated Moe-Di Stefano joint distribution.

populationModels.label: Truncated Raghavan-like birth-period prior
populationModels.applicability: MIST binary candidates within the configured positive orbital-period interval.
populationModels.phaseConvention: No orbital phase: this model samples the fixed birth period only.
limitations: The rounded solar-type field-star log-normal parameters are applied at every primary mass, metallicity, age, and environment.
Configured bounds define a conditional distribution; there are no clipped endpoint atoms, but excluded probability is not represented by a weight correction.
Period, mass ratio, and multiplicity are sampled independently despite observed correlations.

populationModels.label: Magellanic Cloud distance-depth placement
populationModels.applicability: LMC and SMC live-HR source systems, with one line-of-sight distance per system.
equations: D_LMC~Normal(49.59 kpc,(0.75 kpc)^2) conditioned on D_LMC>0
D_SMC~Normal(62.44 kpc,(1.75 kpc)^2) conditioned on D_SMC>0
the chosen 95-percent full line-of-sight depths are approximately 3 kpc (LMC) and 7 kpc (SMC)
populationModels.phaseConvention: Each distance is a deterministic seed, system-ID, and placement-index draw. Both components of a binary share exactly the same indexed distance.
limitations: The cited eclipsing-binary measurements constrain central distances; the Gaussian depth widths are explicit display priors, not their distance uncertainties.
The Clouds' sky-plane extent, inclination, warp, asymmetric SMC depth, tidal structure, and age-dependent geometry are omitted.
Every stellar population and binary configuration within a Cloud uses the same line-of-sight depth law.

populationModels.label: MIST v2.5 Gaia EDR3 synthetic G photometry
populationModels.applicability: Finite MIST v2.5 alpha=0, v/vcrit=0 stellar states whose theoretical isochrone coordinates have an exactly aligned UBVRIplus Gaia_G_EDR3 row at every interpolation corner.
equations: fail closed if a source header, EEP/age/mass key, interpolation corner, or positive finite flux is absent
populationModels.phaseConvention: No time-domain phase is evaluated: this is the mean absolute Gaia EDR3 G magnitude of the selected MIST source state at 10 pc.
limitations: The result inherits MIST atmosphere, stellar-evolution, grid-resolution, and interpolation systematics and is not empirical Gaia photometry.
Only the source Gaia_G_EDR3 Vega magnitude is used; color-dependent calibration corrections and passband uncertainties are omitted.
The source tables have Av=0, so extinction, circumstellar dust, unresolved companions, and time variability are deliberately applied by separate models.
Flux interpolation can blend evolutionary phases; the cross-phase condition is flagged but does not turn the blend into a phase-resolved atmosphere calculation.

populationModels.label: MIST v2.5 isochrone and EEP-track evolution
populationModels.applicability: Finite single-star states whose initial mass, age, and composition are bracketed by the local MIST v2.5 alpha=0, v/vcrit=0 grid.
equations: surface H,He=clip(X_MIST,0,1) only when the excursion is <=1e-8; larger excursions fail closed
WDCS iff EEP>=wd_start_eep(header); terminal iff EEP>=terminal_eep(header)
populationModels.phaseConvention: No variability phase is assigned: age is elapsed time since stellar birth, and EEP orders the corresponding MIST evolutionary history.
limitations: Uses one-dimensional, non-rotating, solar-scaled stellar models and does not represent interacting-binary evolution.
Interpolation can smooth short evolutionary phases and inherits MIST input-physics and grid-resolution systematics.
Discrete phase and EEP labels come from the nearest interpolation corner while continuous fields are blended; cross-phase blends are explicitly flagged.
Tracks end at white-dwarf cooling or carbon burning according to initial mass; states outside certified age, mass, or composition coverage fail closed.

The default birth-metallicity cap is Z=0.0279969 because the +0.50-dex EEP archive does not certify the required low-mass histories through old ages; an explicit higher override can therefore produce fail-closed absent stars or rejected binaries.
A finite terminal EEP is retained and flagged, but the model never extrapolates cooling or any other evolution beyond the grid endpoint.
Atmosphere class and remnant subtype may remain uncertain when the tabulated surface composition or terminal phase is ambiguous.
Published and interpolated surface H/He mass fractions can cross 0 or 1 by floating-point roundoff; only excursions no larger than 1e-8 are canonicalized to the boundary.

populationModels.label: Milky Way age-metallicity prior
populationModels.applicability: Milky Way Live-HR candidate systems after their formation lookback times have been drawn.
equations: Z=0.0142*10^[Fe/H]_proxy, then clip to the configured supported Z interval
populationModels.phaseConvention: One birth composition is drawn after the formation age and is held fixed as the initial composition supplied to MIST.
limitations: The stored [Fe/H] label is the proxy log10(Z/0.0142), not a separately evolved iron abundance.
The one-zone relation omits radial and vertical gradients, alpha enhancement, distinct Galactic components, migration, and correlated chemical scatter.
Metallicity clipping can create probability at a configured support boundary; changing the SFH changes the marginal metallicity distribution even though this conditional relation is unchanged.

populationModels.label: Constant Milky Way star-formation history
populationModels.applicability: Milky Way Live-HR candidate systems over the fixed 0--13.2 Gyr formation-lookback interval.
equations: p(t_lookback)=1/(13.2 Gyr) on the supported interval
populationModels.phaseConvention: Formation lookback time is sampled once at birth; zero is the present and 13.2 Gyr is the oldest supported formation epoch.
limitations: This is an explicit analytic Live-HR prior, not a fit to a reconstructed Milky Way star-formation history.
A single constant history cannot represent the thin disk, thick disk, bulge, halo, radial migration, bursts, or quenching.
Age is sampled independently of birth mass, multiplicity, and spatial position; only the separate age-metallicity relation depends on age.

populationModels.label: Axisymmetric Milky Way exponential-disk placement
populationModels.applicability: Milky Way Live-HR source systems drawn from the registered constant 0--13.2 Gyr formation history.
equations: R~Gamma(k=2,theta=2.6 kpc) conditioned on 0<=R<=20 kpc, equivalently p(R) proportional to R*exp(-R/2.6 kpc)
populationModels.phaseConvention: Each position is a deterministic seed, system-ID, and placement-index draw. Both components of a binary share exactly the same indexed placement.
limitations: This is a one-component display prior, not a complete Milky Way model: the bulge, bar, halo, spiral arms, warp, flare, and substructure are absent.
One radial scale length and one vertical scale height are applied at every age, mass, and metallicity; age-dependent disk heating and population gradients are omitted.
The 20 kpc radial truncation is a numerical support choice rather than a measured sharp disk edge.
The source population's constant one-zone star-formation history cannot predict magnitude-limited bulge or halo counts.

populationModels.label: Smooth Milky Way dust and Gaia-G extinction
populationModels.applicability: Milky Way placements use a smooth exponential dust-disk integral; populations without synthesized sky coordinates use explicit fixed foreground-screen priors.
equations: A_V=3.1*E(B-V); A_G=0.789*A_V; numerical cap A_G<=20 mag
fixed A_G foreground screens: LMC=0.25 mag, SMC=0.15 mag, globular_10gyr=0.30 mag, open_1gyr=0.20 mag
populationModels.phaseConvention: Extinction is static and shared by both components of a system; stellar variability and eclipses never change the dust column.
limitations: The Li et al. fit is a smooth low-latitude average; molecular clouds, the Gould Belt, spiral structure, small-scale angular variation, and modern 3D map information are omitted.
A_G/A_V=0.789 is held fixed although broad-band Gaia extinction depends on source spectrum, extinction, and passband; the cited coefficient was calibrated for Gaia DR2 red-clump stars.
The fixed Cloud and cluster screens are display priors necessitated by missing sky coordinates, not evaluations of the exponential dust integral or predictions for particular sightlines.
Internal Magellanic-Cloud and circumstellar extinction are omitted; the A_G<=20 mag cap is numerical rather than physical.

populationModels.label: Illustrative Plummer cluster placement
populationModels.applicability: The synthetic 10 Gyr globular-cluster and 1 Gyr open-cluster populations.
equations: r=a/sqrt(U^(-2/3)-1), U~Uniform(0,1), for a Plummer sphere
globular_10gyr: D_center=10 kpc and a=3 pc
open_1gyr: D_center=1 kpc and a=2 pc
populationModels.phaseConvention: Each position is a deterministic seed, system-ID, and placement-index draw. Both components of a binary share exactly the same indexed position.
limitations: The cluster distances and scale radii are illustrative placement assumptions, not fits to named observed clusters.
The clusters are weighted simple stellar populations rather than dynamical finite-N realizations; mass segregation, evaporation, binaries' dynamical processing, and tidal truncation are absent.
Only the isotropic line-of-sight offset affects apparent magnitude; no sky coordinates, angular crowding, or cluster membership selection are synthesized.

populationModels.label: Unresolved mean Gaia-G system selection
populationModels.applicability: Photometrically complete synthetic systems with finite component MIST Gaia EDR3 G magnitudes, a positive distance, and finite non-negative Gaia-G extinction.
equations: retain every component of the system iff G_mean<=G_limit; default G_limit=20.7 mag
interactive limits span 8<=G_limit<=22 mag in 0.1 mag steps
populationModels.phaseConvention: No variability or orbital phase enters selection. The same phase-independent mean system magnitude is compared with every limit.
limitations: This is a sharp Gaia-like display cut, not the Gaia selection function: scanning law, detection probability, crowding, color dependence, window assignment, quality cuts, and sky-position completeness are absent.
Every binary is treated as unresolved regardless of projected separation; if any expected component lacks photometry, the whole system fails closed.
Selection uses mean source-state flux and ignores pulsation, flares, orbital modulation, and eclipse phase, so transient threshold crossings are not modeled.
Source weights are admitted or excluded without Vmax correction or renormalization, and the nominal 20.7 mag mission limit is not a claim of uniform catalogue completeness.

populationModels.label: Weighted observed realizations and compact PPS overlay
populationModels.applicability: Photometrically complete weighted source systems convolved with the registered spatial/extinction model; the compact overlay is conditioned on mean unresolved G<=20.7.
equations: prototype i: sum_(k=1..K_i) w_i/K_i = w_i exactly
detected empirical system weight W_i,det=(w_i/K_i)*sum_k I(G_i,k<=20.7)
within mutually exclusive stratum h, systematic PPS uses size W_i,det and interval W_h/n_h
overlay visualization calibration weight=W_h/n_h; it is not an HT or Hansen-Hurwitz analysis weight
K_i=64 for predeclared rare model IDs; K_i=8 otherwise
populationModels.phaseConvention: Placement draw index k is part of the stable random-access identity. Observed realization index independently keys variability and orbital nuisance draws.
limitations: The finite K_i placement ensemble introduces Monte Carlo discretization in detection fractions; a deterministic split-half diagnostic is exported.

Rare-stratum reserves deliberately distort the compact overlay's unweighted class frequencies, so overlay records are noninferential and authoritative weighted counts remain in the full sidecar/audit.
Conditioning the overlay on the default cut means it cannot display systems detectable only at a fainter interactive limit; the sidecar remains authoritative for every supported threshold.
Realizations reuse each prototype's physical MIST state while independently drawing variability phases/noise and binary orientation/epoch nuisance parameters.
